# Turn-Based Mage Roguelike — Design Spec

> A traditional grid roguelike where **movement is casting**.

## Premise

You control a mage 🧙 on a fully-visible 40×24 board. You never aim, select, or cast a
spell. Every spell hangs off a *trigger* (`on-move`, `on-strike`, `on-kill`…), so your
turn is a **routing decision**: which path through the crowd sets off the most magic.

Survive 400 turns.

**Reference points:** [Path of Achra](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1889620/)
(turn-based, auto-triggering build cascades — the closest existing thing to this design)
and [Rift Wizard](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1717070/) (turn-based tactical
wizard, large spell pool). Play Achra before building.

## The loop

Press a direction → your turn resolves instantly → triggers cascade (depth-capped at 3)
→ enemies act per the energy scheduler → animations play over ~100ms **without ever
blocking your next input**.

Kills drop 💎. Walking over gems levels you up. Level-up offers **4 cards** (new spell,
or +1 level to something owned) with **3 rerolls per run**; skip → small heal.

**4 spell slots + 4 passive slots.**

## Player

| | |
|---|---|
| HP | 50 |
| Speed | 1.0 (baseline energy gain) |
| Bump attack | walk into an enemy for chip damage, consumes turn, fires `on-strike` |
| Blink | 4 tiles, 8-turn cooldown, consumes turn, fires `on-blink`, does **not** count as a step |

Blink has exactly one job: escaping a full **surround**, when all eight adjacent tiles
are bodies and movement genuinely cannot solve the problem.

## Spells — 8, mapped to trigger × shape

| Spell | School | Trigger | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✨ Magic Missile *(starting)* | 🔮 Arcane | on-move | Bolt at nearest |
| 🌀 Void Rift | 🔮 Arcane | every 5th step | Ground, pulls adjacent enemies inward |
| 🔥 Fireball | 🔥 Fire | on-strike | Burst r2 on the struck enemy + Burn |
| ☄️ Meteor | 🔥 Fire | every 6th step | Burst r2 on densest cluster, leaves Burning Ground |
| ❄️ Ice Lance | ❄️ Ice | on-move | Beam along the direction you just moved, pierces, Slow |
| 🧊 Frost Nova | ❄️ Ice | on-take-damage | Burst r2 on self, Freeze |
| ⚡ Chain Arc | ⚡ Lightning | **on-kill** | Chain to 3 nearest |
| 🌩️ Static Field | ⚡ Lightning | every 3rd step | Burst r1 (all 8 adjacent) |

- **Chain Arc** is the cascade centrepiece: kills cause chains cause kills.
- **Ice Lance** is the purest expression of the premise — the direction you walk *is* the
  direction you fire.
- **Ground** effects are weak in real time but devastating turn-based: enemies must spend
  turns walking through them, and you can pre-place them on chokepoints.

Each spell has **5 hand-authored behavioural levels** — L3 pierces, L5 changes behaviour.
Not `+15% damage`.

### Grid shapes

`Bolt` (travels a line, hits first enemy) · `Burst` (radius-N around a point or self) ·
`Beam` (instant, whole row/column/diagonal) · `Chain` (hops to nearest enemies N times) ·
`Ground` (persistent damaging tiles for M turns)

### Triggers

`on-move` · `on-Nth-step` · `on-strike` · `on-kill` · `on-take-damage` · `on-blink`

Cascading is enabled: a triggered spell's kills fire `on-kill` spells, which can kill
more. **Hard depth cap of 3 and a per-turn trigger budget** — uncapped mutual triggers
will hard-lock the game.

## Passives — 8

| | |
|---|---|
| 🔥 **Emberheart** | +Fire damage, +Burn duration |
| ❄️ **Frozen Core** | +Ice damage, +Freeze/Slow duration |
| ⚡ **Stormcaller** | +Lightning damage, +1 chain hop |
| 🔮 **Arcane Focus** | +Arcane damage, +1 projectile |
| 📖 **Tome** | −1 to every "every Nth step" counter (the cooldown-reduction analogue — strongest passive in the game) |
| 👟 **Swiftboots** | +speed: you act more often than enemies do |
| 🧲 **Lodestone** | auto-collect gems within N tiles |
| 🛡️ **Ward** | +max HP; blink leaves a damaging rift at your origin (the one `on-blink` effect) |

## Evolutions — 3

Unlocked by taking a spell to L5 **and** maxing its school's passive.

| Recipe | Result |
|---|---|
| 🔥 Fireball + Emberheart | 🌋 **Cataclysm** — Burst r3, and anything it kills explodes again |
| ❄️ Frost Nova + Frozen Core | ❄️ **Absolute Zero** — Burst r4, 2-turn freeze, frozen deaths shatter |
| ⚡ Chain Arc + Stormcaller | 🌪️ **Maelstrom** — chains to 6, and chain kills re-trigger |

## Enemies — melee only, one verb: walk at you

| | Speed | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 🧟 Shambler | 0.75 | baseline body |
| 🦇 Bat | 2.0 — acts twice per your turn | fast swarm, low HP |
| 🪨 Golem | 0.5 — acts every other turn | wall, high HP/damage, immune to pull |
| 💀 Elite | varies | 5× HP, drops 🎁 = instant level + guaranteed rare |

An enemy adjacent to you attacks on its turn. **Adjacency is the telegraph** — perfectly
readable on a grid. No i-frames (meaningless turn-based).

## Arena

40×24 tiles at 32px = 1280×768. Fits exactly on one screen: **no camera, no scrolling,
no fog of war, whole board always visible.**

Scattered impassable pillars 🪨 (~8–10% of tiles). These are load-bearing: with
trigger-based casting, a turn is a routing choice, and an empty rectangle has no
interesting routes to choose between. Pillars create pinch points, safe lanes and traps.

## Timeline — 400 turns

Enemies spawn from **arena edges** on a turn-indexed authored timeline. Directional
pressure is readable and routable on a fully-visible board. Escalation comes from spawn
rate, enemy tier and speed — not raw count. Soft cap ~100 simultaneous enemies.

| Turn | Event |
|---|---|
| 0 | Shamblers trickle, one edge |
| 50 | Bats join, two edges |
| **120** | **Elite** |
| 200 | Golems introduced, **Elite** |
| 200–300 | Heavy mixed, all four edges |
| **300** | **Elite** |
| 300–350 | Golem wall + Bat swarm |
| **350–400** | **THE STORM** — all edges, max rate, tiers maxed |
| 400 | Survive = **win** |

Death ends the run. Nothing persists between runs, but run state is a self-contained
object so meta-progression can be added later without a refactor.

## Presentation

Emoji glyphs, played straight — chosen for **readability first**, humour as a side
effect. No joke text; spell names are sincere.

**Emoji cannot be tinted** (they're colour bitmap glyphs), so all juice lives *around*
them: glow blobs and shadows drawn underneath, particles, squash/stretch/rotation of the
glyph, screenshake, floating damage numbers.

The animation layer is **functional, not decorative**. When one step sets off a cascade
of five spells, the staggered playback *is* how the player understands what their build
just did.

**No audio in the prototype.**

## Tech

- **TypeScript + Vite + Canvas 2D.** No engine.
- **Energy-based turn scheduler** — every actor accrues energy per tick and acts when it
  has enough. Speed is a real stat, which is what makes Ice's slow the strongest effect
  in the game (fewer enemy turns, not slower movement).
- **Dijkstra flow field** toward the player, recomputed each turn. Handles any number of
  enemies and any obstacle layout without per-enemy pathfinding.
- Grid occupancy arrays.
- **Non-blocking animation queue** — the model resolves the instant you press a key;
  visuals catch up and compress or snap if you press again. Blocking animation is the
  single most common way turn-based roguelikes feel bad, and it gets exponentially worse
  with long cascades.
- Cascade depth cap 3 + per-turn trigger budget.
- **Seeded RNG** + `?seed=` URL param for reproducible runs.
- **F1 debug overlay**: turn counter, entity counts, force level-up, spawn arbitrary
  enemy, god mode, single-step, **cascade log**.
- All content (spells, passives, enemies, timeline) in **typed TS data modules** — no
  parsing layer, full autocomplete and type-checking.

## Build order

1. Grid, renderer, movement, energy scheduler, debug overlay, seeded RNG
2. Enemies, flow-field pathing, bump attack, melee damage, death
3. **Magic Missile alone, polished until one step feels great** — animation queue, damage
   numbers, particles, shake
4. Gems, XP, level-up card UI with placeholder upgrades
5. Trigger/cascade engine + all 8 spells, 8 passives, 3 evolutions
6. Spawn timeline, elites, chests
7. The Storm, win/lose screens
8. Balance passes

Step 3 is load-bearing: the entire game is "you take a step and something dies." If that
one interaction doesn't feel good, eight spells won't fix it — they'll just be eight
mediocre interactions. It also establishes the juice vocabulary the other seven inherit.

## Risks on the record

1. **Camping.** Turn-based has no clock — nothing forces you to move. Edge spawns and
   floor gems should pull you out, but if playtesting shows people turtling in a pillar
   nook, the design has failed at its core tension. Fix is ready: **gems decay after N
   turns**. Watch for this first.
2. **Cascades are both the fun and the bug source.** The depth cap, trigger budget and
   cascade log are day-one requirements, not polish. Uncapped mutual triggers will
   hard-lock within an hour of authoring spells.
3. **One enemy verb.** Everything just walks at you; all variety must come from spells and
   movement. That's a clean test of the core — but if it feels monotonous, the first fix
   is a telegraphed AoE enemy.
4. **No audio.** Roughly half of "juice" is sound. Careful not to over-correct by piling
   on visual effects to compensate for something silence is causing.

## Explicitly deferred

Meta-progression · multiple characters · a shop/economy · boss fights · ranged or
telegraphed enemy attacks · summons · dungeon floors and level generation · fog of war ·
cross-school elemental reactions · audio.

# Tickets

Vertical slices for the prototype described in [DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md). Each ticket cuts
a complete path from input through model to screen, and each is demoable on its own.
Numbered in dependency order — blockers always appear above the tickets they gate.

## Dependency graph

```
01 skeleton + arena
 └─ 02 movement + scheduler
     └─ 03 debug overlay
         └─ 04 enemies + pathing
             └─ 05 combat
                 ├─ 06 enemy roster + statuses ──┐
                 └─ 07 animation + juice         │
                     └─ 08 triggers + Missile    │
                         ├─ 09 blink ────────┐   │
                         ├─ 10 XP + cards ───┼───┤
                         └─ 11 cascades ─────┤   │
                                             │   │
                             12 spells ◀─────┴───┘
                              └─ 13 passives + evolutions ─┐
                             14 timeline + elites ─────────┤
                                                           │
                                        15 storm + win/lose ◀
                                         └─ 16 balance pass
```

Tickets **06** and **07** can run in parallel. So can **09**, **10** and **11**. Everything
else is a chain.

---

# 01: Project skeleton and seeded arena

**What to build:** running the dev server opens a browser showing the 40×24 arena — floor
tiles and scattered impassable pillars 🪨 — filling a 1280×768 canvas with no scrolling.
Adding `?seed=abc` to the URL produces a specific pillar layout; the same seed always
produces the same layout, a different seed produces a different one.

**Blocked by:** None (can start immediately)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Vite + TypeScript project runs with a single dev command
- [ ] Canvas is 1280×768, grid is 40×24 tiles at 32px, no camera or scrolling
- [ ] Emoji glyphs render legibly and centred in their tiles
- [ ] All randomness flows through one seeded generator; no bare `Math.random` anywhere
- [ ] `?seed=` sets the seed; absent seed picks one and displays it so a run can be replayed
- [ ] Pillar layout is generated from the seed at roughly 8–10% of tiles, leaving the board
      fully connected (no walled-off regions)

---

# 02: Player movement and the energy scheduler

**What to build:** a mage 🧙 stands in the arena. Pressing a direction moves them one tile
in any of eight directions; pillars and arena edges block movement. Every accepted move
advances the world by one turn through an energy-based scheduler, and the current turn
number is visible on screen.

**Blocked by:** 01

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Eight-directional movement via keyboard, with the diagonals reachable
- [ ] Moving into a pillar or the arena edge is rejected and does **not** consume a turn
- [ ] Turn advancement runs through an energy scheduler where each actor accrues energy per
      tick and acts when it has enough — not a hardcoded "player then everyone else" loop
- [ ] Player speed is a data value the scheduler reads, not a constant baked into the loop
- [ ] Turn counter is visible and increments once per accepted action

---

# 03: Debug overlay and single-step control

**What to build:** F1 toggles an overlay showing turn number, actor counts and frame time,
with god mode and a single-step mode that freezes the simulation until you advance it
manually. This is the tool you'll use to diagnose every later ticket, so it lands before
there's much to diagnose.

**Blocked by:** 02

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] F1 toggles the overlay without disturbing the run
- [ ] Overlay reports turn number, actor counts by type, and frame time
- [ ] God mode toggle makes the player untargetable and unkillable
- [ ] Single-step mode halts the scheduler and advances exactly one turn on a keypress
- [ ] Overlay is built so later tickets can register their own readouts and dev actions into
      it rather than each inventing their own debug UI

---

# 04: Enemies and flow-field pathing

**What to build:** shamblers 🧟 spawned from the debug overlay walk toward the player each
turn, routing around pillars rather than getting stuck on them. Enemies occupy tiles and
cannot stack or walk through each other.

**Blocked by:** 03

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Debug overlay can spawn an enemy at a chosen or random location
- [ ] Enemy movement is driven by a Dijkstra flow field toward the player, recomputed each
      turn — no per-enemy pathfinding
- [ ] Enemies route correctly around pillars and never wedge permanently against one
- [ ] Tile occupancy is enforced: one actor per tile, and enemies path around each other
- [ ] Performance holds with 100 simultaneous enemies on the board

---

# 05: Combat — bump attack, melee damage, death

**What to build:** walking into an enemy attacks it for chip damage instead of moving, and
consumes the turn. An enemy standing adjacent to you attacks on its own turn. Both sides
have HP, both can die; enemy death removes it from the board and player death ends the run
with a minimal game-over state.

**Blocked by:** 04

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Moving into an enemy performs a bump attack, deals chip damage, and consumes the turn
- [ ] An enemy adjacent to the player attacks on its turn; adjacency is the only telegraph
- [ ] Player and enemies both carry HP; current player HP is visible
- [ ] Enemy death removes it from the board and frees its tile
- [ ] Player death halts the run and shows a game-over state with turn count reached
- [ ] Damage values come from typed data, not literals in combat code

---

# 06: Enemy roster and status effects

**What to build:** three enemy types with genuinely different speeds — 🧟 Shambler (0.75),
🦇 Bat (2.0, acts twice per player turn), 🪨 Golem (0.5, acts every other turn) — plus a
status-effect system that can slow, freeze and burn an actor. Slowing something visibly
reduces how often it acts.

**Blocked by:** 05

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] All three enemy types exist with distinct speed, HP and damage defined in typed data
- [ ] Speed genuinely changes action frequency through the scheduler; a Bat acts twice per
      player turn and a Golem every other turn
- [ ] Status system supports Slow (reduced energy gain), Freeze (skips turns) and Burn
      (damage over time), each with a duration in turns
- [ ] Statuses are visible on affected actors at a glance
- [ ] Debug overlay can apply any status to any actor for testing
- [ ] Golem is immune to forced movement, ready for the pull effects in ticket 12

---

# 07: Animation queue and the juice vocabulary

**What to build:** the same combat as ticket 05, but it feels good. Moves lerp between
tiles, hits shake and flash, damage numbers float up, particles fire on death. Critically,
**input is never blocked** — pressing a direction mid-animation resolves the next turn
immediately and the pending animation compresses or snaps.

**Blocked by:** 05

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Model resolves a turn the instant input arrives; visuals are a separate catch-up layer
- [ ] Holding or spamming a direction key stays fully responsive with no input lag or queue
      backlog — animations compress or snap rather than gating input
- [ ] Movement lerps, hits shake, deaths emit particles, damage numbers float and fade
- [ ] Glyphs squash/stretch and rotate; glow and shadow are drawn *under* the emoji, since
      emoji themselves cannot be tinted
- [ ] Reusable helpers exist for shake, particle burst and number popup, so later tickets
      inherit the vocabulary rather than reinventing it
- [ ] Animation queue can play a staggered sequence of events, ready for cascades

---

# 08: Trigger engine and the first spell

**What to build:** the tracer bullet for the entire game. A trigger engine that fires
registered effects in response to events, with exactly one trigger (`on-move`) and one
spell wired through it: ✨ Magic Missile, a Bolt at the nearest enemy, firing every time
you take a step. Taking a single step and watching something die should feel great.

**Blocked by:** 07

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Trigger engine dispatches events to registered effects; the event vocabulary is
      extensible without touching the dispatcher
- [ ] `on-move` fires on every accepted step and not on rejected moves or blocked input
- [ ] Bolt shape resolves along a grid line and hits the first enemy it reaches
- [ ] Magic Missile auto-selects the nearest valid enemy with no player input
- [ ] Spell definition lives in typed data — trigger, shape, damage, targeting — with none
      of it hardcoded into the engine
- [ ] The whole loop is animated through ticket 07's queue and feels good at speed
- [ ] Debug overlay reports what fired this turn

---

# 09: Blink

**What to build:** a keypress teleports the mage up to 4 tiles, consumes the turn, and goes
on an 8-turn cooldown shown on screen. It fires an `on-blink` trigger event that nothing
yet listens to. Its purpose is escaping a full surround, so it must work when every
adjacent tile is occupied.

**Blocked by:** 08

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Blink teleports up to 4 tiles in a chosen direction, landing on the furthest legal
      tile if the full distance is blocked
- [ ] Consumes the turn and enters an 8-turn cooldown; cooldown state is visible
- [ ] Works when the player is fully surrounded — this is the ability's entire purpose
- [ ] Fires `on-blink` but does **not** fire `on-move` or advance the step counter, so it
      can't be farmed for step-based procs
- [ ] Distinct teleport animation at both origin and destination

---

# 10: XP gems, leveling and the card screen

**What to build:** dead enemies drop 💎 on the floor. Walking over a gem collects it;
enough gems level you up, which interrupts play with a screen offering 4 cards. You get 3
rerolls per run, and skipping heals a little. Cards can be placeholder stat bumps — this
ticket delivers the *loop*, not the content.

**Blocked by:** 08

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Enemies drop gems on death; gems persist on the floor and are collected by walking over
- [ ] XP accumulates toward a level threshold curve defined in typed data
- [ ] Leveling interrupts with a card screen offering 4 choices
- [ ] 3 rerolls per run, tracked and displayed; skip is available and grants a small heal
- [ ] Card screen respects the 4 spell / 4 passive slot caps and offers upgrade-only cards
      once slots are full
- [ ] Debug overlay can force a level-up
- [ ] Collecting a gem does not cost a turn beyond the move itself

---

# 11: Cascades and the full trigger set

**What to build:** the rest of the trigger vocabulary — `on-Nth-step`, `on-strike`,
`on-kill`, `on-take-damage` — plus cascading, where a triggered spell's kills fire further
triggers. Bounded by a hard depth cap of 3 and a per-turn trigger budget, with a cascade
log in the debug overlay so you can read what happened.

**Blocked by:** 08

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] All six triggers dispatch correctly: `on-move`, `on-Nth-step`, `on-strike`, `on-kill`,
      `on-take-damage`, `on-blink`
- [ ] Step counters for `on-Nth-step` are per-spell and survive across turns
- [ ] Cascades fire: a triggered kill dispatches `on-kill`, which can trigger further effects
- [ ] Hard depth cap of 3 and a per-turn trigger budget, both enforced and configurable
- [ ] Two mutually-triggering effects terminate safely instead of hard-locking the game —
      test this explicitly, it is the single most likely way this system breaks
- [ ] Cascade log in the debug overlay shows the ordered chain of what fired and why
- [ ] Cascades play back as a staggered animated sequence, readable at a glance

---

# 12: Grid shapes and the remaining seven spells

**What to build:** the four shapes beyond Bolt — Burst, Beam, Chain and Ground — and the
seven spells built on them, each with five hand-authored behavioural levels. After this
ticket a run can produce a genuinely different build depending on what you draw.

**Blocked by:** 06, 10, 11

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Burst (radius-N around a point or self), Beam (instant row/column/diagonal), Chain
      (hops to N nearest), and Ground (persistent damaging tiles for M turns) all implemented
- [ ] Ground effects persist across turns, damage anything standing on them, and are visible
- [ ] All 8 spells implemented per the spec table, including Void Rift's inward pull, Ice
      Lance firing along the direction just moved, and Chain Arc firing on kill
- [ ] Each spell has 5 hand-authored levels where levels change *behaviour*, not just numbers
- [ ] Spells apply the appropriate statuses from ticket 06 (Burn, Slow, Freeze)
- [ ] Card screen offers real spells and real upgrades in place of ticket 10's placeholders
- [ ] Chain Arc plus a crowd produces a visible, readable cascade

---

# 13: Passives and evolutions

**What to build:** the 8 passives, including Tome reducing every step-counter by 1 and
Swiftboots raising player speed through the scheduler. Plus the 3 evolutions — taking a
spell to L5 with its school passive maxed transforms it into a distinctly different final
form, announced as a moment.

**Blocked by:** 09, 12

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] All 8 passives implemented and offered on the card screen
- [ ] School-boosting passives correctly scale only their own school's spells
- [ ] Tome reduces every `on-Nth-step` counter; Swiftboots changes player speed via the
      scheduler; Lodestone auto-collects gems in radius; Ward raises max HP and attaches a
      damaging rift to `on-blink`
- [ ] All 3 evolutions trigger on their exact recipe (spell L5 + matching school passive
      maxed) and replace the base spell
- [ ] Evolution is announced with a distinct, unmissable moment
- [ ] Cataclysm's kill-chains and Maelstrom's re-triggering chains stay inside the cascade
      caps from ticket 11

---

# 14: Spawn timeline, elites and chests

**What to build:** enemies stop being debug-spawned and start arriving from the arena edges
on the authored 400-turn timeline — rising rate, new types introduced, escalating tiers.
Elites 💀 appear at turns 120, 200 and 300 and drop chests 🎁 granting an instant level and
a guaranteed rare card.

**Blocked by:** 06, 10

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Spawning is driven by a turn-indexed timeline in typed data, editable without touching
      engine code
- [ ] Enemies enter from arena edges; which edges are active changes over the run and is
      readable from the board
- [ ] Escalation comes from spawn rate, enemy tier and speed rather than raw count, with a
      soft cap around 100 simultaneous enemies
- [ ] Elites spawn on schedule as visually distinct high-HP variants
- [ ] Elite death drops a chest that grants an instant level plus a guaranteed rare card
- [ ] Debug overlay can jump the run to an arbitrary turn to test late-game pressure without
      replaying the early game

---

# 15: The Storm, win and lose, run reset

**What to build:** the run has an ending. Turns 350–400 are a maximum-pressure spike from
every edge, and surviving to turn 400 is a win with a results screen. Death is a loss with
the same screen. One keypress starts a fresh run, and the previous run leaves nothing
behind.

**Blocked by:** 13, 14

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Turns 350–400 run the authored Storm: all edges, maximum rate, maximum tiers
- [ ] Surviving to turn 400 ends the run as a win
- [ ] Win and loss both show a results screen with turns survived, kills, level reached and
      final build
- [ ] Results screen shows the run's seed so it can be replayed exactly
- [ ] One keypress restarts into a fresh run with no state leaking from the previous one
- [ ] Run state is a single self-contained object, so persistent meta-progression can be
      added later without restructuring

---

# 16: First balance pass

**What to build:** a run that is actually winnable but not trivially so, tuned by playing
it repeatedly with the seed and turn-jump tooling. This is where the design's stated risks
get tested against reality rather than argued about.

**Blocked by:** 15

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] A competent player wins a meaningful fraction of runs, and a careless one loses
- [ ] At least three distinctly different builds are viable paths to a win
- [ ] The Storm is genuinely threatening to a maxed build rather than a formality
- [ ] **Camping check:** verify that turtling in a pillar nook is not a winning strategy. If
      it is, the design's core tension has failed — the prepared fix is gems decaying after N
